articles.title: In 1892, Everton left their landlord with an empty stadium over a rent dispute, so he started a football club just to fill it. That club has since won more titles than any other in English football
articles.summary: Football News: Discover the fascinating history of Liverpool FC's origins, born from a rent dispute with Everton FC, and how the rivalry shaped English football. Learn about the rise of both clubs and their impact on the sport.
articles.body: Merseyside's oldest rivalry likes to present itself as a story about football, about who has bragging rights to a city split down the middle. But strip away 130 years of scarves and songs and what's left is a much smaller and pettier story about a landlord who refused to negotiate a rent increase and ended up owning a stadium built for a club that wasn't his anymore.The story stretches back to 1884, when Everton moved into Anfield and turned what was then a developing patch of land into their new home. Eight years later, Everton left for Goodison Park after a bitter disagreement with John Houlding, the club's president and the man who owned Anfield. Houlding was left with a stadium but no football team, and the solution he came up with would change English football forever.The club he created to keep Anfield occupied was Liverpool Football Club.Everton were at Anfield long before Liverpool existedEverton's origins can be traced to 1878, when the club was formed from the football team associated with St Domingo's Church, initially playing at Stanley Park before moving to Priory Road as crowds grew.The move to Priory Road did not last particularly long because the landowner became unhappy with the noise and unruly behaviour surrounding Everton matches, particularly after the club's 1884 Liverpool Cup success. Everton therefore needed another home, and that search took them to Anfield later that year.The ground was initially leased from local brewers John and Richard Orrell, while Everton's president John Houlding subsequently bought the land outright in 1885. Everton played their first match at Anfield against Earlestown on September 27, 1884, winning 5-0.Anfield quickly became an important part of Everton's early rise, with the club becoming professional while based there and hosting its first Football League fixture against Accrington Stanley on September 8, 1888.The biggest moment came in the 1890-91 season, when Everton won their first English championship at Anfield, attracting crowds of up to 20,000 as they established themselves among the country's leading clubs.At that point, there was little reason to believe Anfield would eventually become synonymous with a completely different club.The rent dispute that changed Merseyside footballThe relationship between Houlding and Everton's committee gradually deteriorated as the club's success and popularity increased, but the dispute was complicated by Houlding's unusual position within Everton's structure.He was not simply the club's landlord. Houlding had become involved with Everton during their search for a new home, served as the club's president, and eventually acquired Anfield himself in 1885, after the land passed from its original owner, brewer John Orrell. That left him occupying two roles at once: he was both a leading figure within Everton and the private owner from whom the club rented its stadium.For a time, that arrangement appeared convenient for everyone. Houlding could support the club while benefiting from the growing value of the ground, and Everton had a secure home in which their crowds and reputation continued to expand. As the club became more successful, however, the arrangement created an increasingly difficult conflict between Houlding's interests as president and his interests as Anfield's owner.Houlding wanted Everton to commit to a financial arrangement that he believed properly reflected the ground's rising value, while members of the club's committee wanted a long-term rental agreement on terms they considered more reasonable. The rent had risen from £100 a year in 1884 to £250 by 1892, and the committee also resisted Houlding's preference for selling the ground to the club rather than continuing with a conventional lease.The disagreement became increasingly bitter because neither side viewed the issue as merely a routine business negotiation. Houlding believed he had helped establish Everton at Anfield and was entitled to benefit from the ground's success, while the committee feared that the club was becoming financially dependent on one individual who controlled both its home and its leadership.Eventually, the two sides could no longer remain together.On March 15, 1892, Houlding and his allies formally split from Everton after the dispute reached breaking point. Everton moved across Stanley Park to Mere Green Field, which would become Goodison Park, leaving Anfield without the club that had occupied it for eight years.Goodison Park officially opened on August 24, 1892, with 12,000 people attending the ceremony, and Everton have remained associated with the ground ever since.Houlding, meanwhile, had a rather different problem.He still had Anfield, but there was no longer a team playing there.An empty Anfield led to Liverpool Football ClubRather than allow his ground to sit unused, Houlding and a group of associates set about creating a new football club that could make Anfield its home.The process began in March 1892, with Houlding and his associates establishing the foundations of the new club after their split from Everton. William E. Barclay was credited with suggesting the name Liverpool, while the new organisation was initially known as Liverpool Football Club and Athletic Grounds Limited.By the time Liverpool was formally registered on June 3, 1892, Everton had already moved across Stanley Park and begun establishing themselves at Goodison Park. Liverpool then took over Anfield, creating the impression in later retellings that the two clubs had once shared the ground. In reality, Everton's departure came first, and Liverpool's arrival followed as the direct consequence of it.That sequence gives the story its peculiar force. Liverpool did not grow out of a shared stadium or emerge as a second club alongside Everton; it was created to occupy the ground Everton had abandoned after the rent dispute. One of English football's greatest clubs began because another club decided it no longer wanted to play at the same address.Liverpool spent their first season in the Lancashire League before entering the Football League's second tier in 1893, beginning a journey that would eventually take them to the very top of English and European football.The club Everton created by leaving Anfield became an English giantThere is a particularly neat symmetry to what happened next because the club that was born from Everton's departure eventually became one of the most decorated teams in English football.Liverpool have now won 20 English top-flight league titles, with their latest championship coming under Arne Slot in 2024-25, taking them level with Manchester United for the all-time record. They have also won six European Cups, with their European triumphs coming in 1977, 1978, 1981, 1984, 2005 and 2019.Everton's own history remains substantial, even if their trophy cabinet has not kept pace with their neighbours.The Toffees have won nine English top-flight championships, five FA Cups and the 1984-85 European Cup-Winners' Cup, while their most recent major honour was the 1995 FA Cup. Their nine league titles remain a significant part of the club's history, with the first coming at Anfield in 1890-91That means the stadium where Everton won their first league championship eventually became the home of the club that would go on to equal the English record for top-flight titles.The irony becomes difficult to miss.Liverpool and Everton nearly came together againMore than a century after Everton left Anfield, the two clubs came surprisingly close to reversing the separation that created their rivalry in the first place.In the early 2000s, Liverpool and Everton were involved in discussions about the possibility of sharing a new stadium, with Liverpool exploring plans for a 60,000-seat ground in Stanley Park while Everton were also considering their own stadium options. Liverpool City Council and the Northwest Development Agency encouraged the clubs to consider the economic and regeneration benefits of a joint project.The idea never developed into a shared home, but it returned in a much more unusual form around 2010.The Mersey Stadia-Connex Group proposed a bizarre "Siamese-style" stadium, essentially two separate grounds joined together by a central spine. The proposal envisaged a 60,000-seat stadium for Liverpool alongside a 50,000-seat stadium for Everton, allowing the clubs to retain separate identities while sharing infrastructure and potentially saving around £200 million.The proposed complex was even more ambitious than simply putting two football grounds next to one another, with plans including 150 executive boxes, a 300-bed hotel and an underground car park capable of holding 1,350 vehicles.The project was also linked to hopes of strengthening Liverpool's prospects in England's bid to host the 2018 World Cup, although the tournament was ultimately awarded to Russia.Neither club ultimately pursued the idea.Liverpool eventually chose to remain at Anfield and expand their historic home, while Everton pursued their own move away from Goodison Park to Bramley-Moore Dock.The result is that the two clubs remain neighbours, but with separate homes and a rivalry that has survived every change in football around them.And that brings the story back to where it began: Anfield.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Los deberes del Sevilla en la recta final de mercado
articles.standfirst: El club necesita cerrar tres fichajes como mínimo, pero cada vez le quedan menos opciones
articles.summary: El club necesita cerrar tres fichajes como mínimo, pero cada vez le quedan menos opciones
articles.body: A menos de dos días para que cierre el mercado de traspasos, el Sevilla vuelve a vivir unas horas frenéticas en los despachos, con muchos frentes abiertos para la Dirección Deportiva encabezada por José Ignacio Navarro. Pese a que la contundente derrota contra el Atlético de Madrid no alteró la hoja de ruta de la planificación, sí que puso de manifiesto las costuras de una plantilla que no solo anda muy escasa de recursos, sino que debe lidiar con una preocupante falta de profundidad en el banquillo. "El plan lo tendrá que decidir la dirección deportiva, ellos ya saben lo que yo pienso", declaró Luis García Plaza después del partido contra los colchoneros. En estos últimos días, el entrenador madrileño ha mostrado su descontento en diversas ocasiones, pues es plenamente consciente de que el equipo necesita reforzarse a contrarreloj para no pasar tantos apuros como en los cursos anteriores. Demasiadas incógnitas en el aire y cada vez menos tiempo de reacción. El margen salarial del Sevilla es aún limitado. Con la venta de Oso al Estrasburgo por 10 millones de euros, solo puede reinvertir aproximadamente unos 2 millones de lo ingresado. Por tanto, se mantiene abierta la operación salida para acudir al mercado con cierta solvencia. En este sentido, la clave continúa siendo Rubén Vargas, excluido de las dos convocatorias ligueras. Olympiacos no llega a los 15 millones que piden por él en Nervión, mientras que el internacional suizo alterna entrenamientos con el grupo y en solitario a la espera de resolver su situación. El ahorro de su ficha permitiría acometer entre dos y tres incorporaciones. Además de Rubén Vargas, el Sevilla pretende traspasar a Fábio Cardoso, apartado del equipo desde el inicio de la pretemporada. En el caso de no encontrarle acomodo al defensa portugués, podría plantearse incluso una rescisión de contrato, como ya ocurrió el pasado verano con Kelechi Iheanacho. Otro de los que podría salir es Marcao, si bien a estas alturas del mercado se antoja complicado. En el contexto actual, tampoco es descartable la venta de alguna pieza importante de la plantilla si llega una oferta irrechazable, como podría ser el caso de Lucien Agoumé. En el apartado de fichajes, la prioridad del cuerpo técnico pasa por firmar a un delantero centro. Luis García Plaza ha dejado claro que desea al menos contar con la posibilidad de alinear a dos puntas desde el inicio, un escenario imposible en estos momentos al disponer únicamente de Isaac Romero y del recién llegado Robbie Ure. De hecho, las decisiones del técnico dejan a las claras que el lebrijano no le convence como única referencia ofensiva. El abanico de candidatos se ha ido desgranando a toda velocidad durante estas semanas. El preferido para la dirección deportiva, George Ilenikhena, queda prácticamente descartado ante las exigencias económicas de Al-Ittihad, que exige un traspaso que el Sevilla no puede afrontar. Mucho más factible resultaba el segundo en la lista, Conrad Harder, al que pretendía traer a préstamo del RB Leipzig. Sin embargo, el danés ha terminado decantándose por el Estrasburgo, obligando así a cambiar de estrategia. Ante la negativa de Harder, el Sevilla ha retomado el interés en Petar Ratkov, por el que inició contactos con la Lazio la pasada semana. La entidad hispalense ha vuelto a plantearse su cesión, pero el Levante y el Toulouse han tomado ventaja, hasta el punto de que el internacional serbio podría haber aceptado ya la propuesta granota. Al margen de otras alternativas en las que se viene trabajando, en la recámara sigue estando la vía de la agencia libre, donde aún esperan jugadores como Joselu. El extremo es la otra demarcación marcada en rojo para el Sevilla. Algunos de los que han sonado este verano, como Bryan Zaragoza, Exequiel Zeballos o Robinho Júnior, ya han elegido destino. Por ello, en las últimas horas ha cobrado fuerza el nombre del sueco Isak Bjerkebo. El extremo zurdo del Sirius y excompañero de Robbie Ure gusta mucho por su proyección y movilidad, aunque el PSV también se ha interesado en su fichaje. Por su parte, su equipo se ha cubierto las espaldas firmando en su posición a Zalán Vancsa. La opción mediática para la banda sería Leon Bailey, al que le resta un año de contrato en el Aston Villa. Los villanos sopesan renovarlo antes de cederlo tras su préstamo a la Roma. Eso sí, su elevada ficha es un obstáculo gigantesco, de modo que su club tendría que asumir como mínimo dos tercios de su salario con tal de que encaje en la economía sevillista. Asimismo, sobre la mesa aparecen otras oportunidades como Bryan Gil (Girona), Gabri Martínez (Sporting de Braga) o el ofrecimiento de Tay Abed (Levante). En el centro del campo, el Sevilla apenas cuenta con Jon Guridi, Lucien Agoumé y Giorgi Kochorashvili, además de los canteranos Manu Bueno y Nico Guillén. El mexicano Obed Vargas, cuya llegada parecía encarrilada hasta hace unos días, ha elegido al Getafe. Ahora los focos apuntan a Soungoutou Magassa, futbolista franco-maliense del West Ham que puede actuar tanto en la medular como en el eje de la zaga. Los nervionenses negocian una cesión con obligación de compra, oferta similar a la que habría presentado el Bolonia. Otros posibles centrocampistas que se han relacionado con el Sevilla son Melayro Bogarde (LASK Link), por el que pedirían 9 millones de euros, o Renato Sanches (PSG), ofrecido por Jorge Mendes y que podría facilitar la marcha de Fábio Cardoso. La llegada de un defensa central queda supeditada precisamente al adiós del portugués o el de Marcao. Sin ellos, el primer equipo blanquirrojo apenas contaría con dieciocho fichas profesionales. En definitiva, al Sevilla le espera otra recta final de mercado de máxima tensión, donde los movimientos en la rampa de salida condicionarán el margen de maniobra de cara a las entradas. El equipo ha demostrado tener alma y compromiso en el arranque liguero, pero en estos momentos carece de los mimbres necesarios para poder afrontar la temporada con ciertas garantías.

articles.standfirst: Tres derrotas en tres partidos de inicio. Romero dice estar tranquilo
articles.summary: Tres derrotas en tres partidos de inicio. Romero dice estar tranquilo
articles.body: El equipo caballa, tal como ocurriera el pasado curso en el ascenso a la categoría después de 45 años, ha perdido sus tres primeros partidos de liga. Si el año pasado lo hiciera ante Valladolid, Sporting y Racing de Santander, en este caso Andorra, Las Palmas y Mallorca han sido los verdugos de los de José Juan Romero. El entrenador del equipo caballa se muestra tranquilo y aseguró tras la tercera derrota consecutiva que tiene sensaciones "muchísimo mejores que la pasada temporada", pero sobre el terreno de juego los números dicen lo contrario, con un Ceuta mucho menos incisivo que el año pasado, cuando puso contra las cuerdas al Sporting y Racing. Aunque Romero no quiere hablar de "excusas", sí es cierto que al Ceuta no le ha acompañado la suerte en estos inicios ligueros, con una situación social por la inmigración descontrolada que está afectando a los diferentes sectores de la ciudad, incluyendo el fútbol, y que ha provocado dificultades al equipo a la hora de buscar refuerzos. Por otro lado está el plano de las lesiones. Omar Sadik no ha podido jugar dos de los tres partidos, y Kenneth Mamah, otro de los fichajes del equipo caballa, se ha lesionado de larga duración sin que el club haya dado los motivos. Para colmo de males, Marino se lesionó en el calentamiento ante el Mallorca, y Anuar se tuvo que retirar comenzado el partido también con molestias. El Ceuta ya prepara la primera visita del filial del Celta de Vigo este fin de semana al Murube, en donde los caballas intentarán quitarse de encima las malas sensaciones en busca de sus primeros puntos en liga.

articles.body: El PSG puede respirar tranquilo. Su principal estrella, Ousmane Dembélé, está a punto de renovar un contrato que le ligaría al conjunto parisino hasta junio de 2030. Todo parece listo para que el vigente campeón del Balón de Oro selle su firma en su nuevo contrato tal y como informan desde Canal + Francia. Dos años más de relación entre Dembélé y PSG, lo que cortará de raíz cualquier rumor de una posible salida. Porque este mismo verano se especuló con que el jugador podría haber sido tentado por el fútbol árabe. Sin embargo, esta mejora salarial, unida a que el futbolista se siente agradecido al club y al gran proyecto deportivo que hay, con dos Champions consecutivas, han terminado de convencer al 'Mosquito'. El equipo que dirige Luis Enrique celebra así una excelente noticia. El técnico asturiano sabe que el jugador es uno de sus pilares fundamentales. articles.title: Mary Earps exclusive: London City Lionesses goalkeeper on busy summer transfer window and facing Man Utd in WSL opener
articles.summary: Mary Earps joined London City Lionesses this summer and was followed by the likes of Alexia Putellas, Mapi Leon and Kadidiatou Diani; watch London City Lionesses vs Man Utd on the opening weekend of the WSL season on September 4, live on Sky Sports; kick-off 7pm
articles.body:
The goalkeeper returns to the WSL after a two-year spell in France with PSG, something she describes as 'a very different environment'.

Speaking exclusively to Sky Sports ahead of the WSL's return on September 4, when London City face her former side, Manchester United, Earps said: "I really feel like I was able to go away and work on myself for a couple of years. There were things in my game that I've been able to kind work on as well.

"As a person, living away from home, immersing yourself in a new language, in a new culture, a new city, a new country, it teaches you a lot of things about yourself. It gives you space to reflect and figure out more about who you are and who you want to be as a person."

Earps has never been afraid of the big move. She also played for German giants Wolfsburg for a year before joining Man Utd and it's that experience that gives her empathy for the players coming to England.

"There's people who are maybe moving clubs for the first time," she said. "There's people moving countries, speaking different languages. I know how hard that is, but even moving back to England and speaking English, it's still a transition."

And the list of players now at London City is eye-watering. The biggest is Alexia Putellas - the Ballon d'Or winner who left her childhood club Barcelona for Bromley. Her team-mate Mapi Leon followed, as has Kadidiatou Diani. That's before we even talk about the players already there, like Kosovare Asllani, Delphine Cascarino and Grace Geyoro.

While these players, Earps included, are used to superstardom, they are still the newbies - dauting for anyone - but such an experience fosters a comradery vital for a successful team.

The goalkeeper explained: "I feel very much part of the newness of it all, and it's nice when other people are experiencing that for the first time as well, but even the players that have been here before, they've maybe only been here a year or so.

"But that's what happens when you're a brand new entity and it's exciting because you get to be a part of that history, and I do believe that London City will go on to do incredible things for a long time. That's a massive reason why I came here.

"It's great in a way because it's like everyone's first day at school. You say 'oh, I'm so nervous', but everyone is nervous because everyone's doing the same thing.

"But there's a lot of experience in the room as well. A lot of the players have won trophies, have incredible pedigree, so we're all bonded by that experience and maybe bumping into each other or playing against each other in some way.

"I honestly can't speak highly enough of the group that I've experienced so far and they've been brilliant at welcoming me."

It's not yet clear if Earps will be the London City No1. She will likely fight for the shirt alongside last season's first choice, Elene Lete - who signed a new deal this summer - with Sophia Poor and Sophie Hillyerd also among the goalkeeping group.

London City will want to tighten up at the back too, conceding 35 WSL goals last season. Not the worst, but for context, the top two - Manchester City and Arsenal - conceded 33 between them. Chelsea only let in 20, and if the club has any ambitions of unseating the Big Three, their number needs to dramatically reduce.

So how does the former WSL Golden Glove winner go about building that solidity with her new defenders?

"It's getting to know them because every individual is so different," Earps explained. "It's a lot of small details which make a big difference.

"Full-back and centre-back are two very different positions. Then you've got everyone's individual qualities and that is probably the hardest part - getting to know things like their starting positions, how they want to do the recovery runs, what position they going to take up in the box or how they like to receive the ball - do they like it in front of them, at them? Are they going to take two steps forward?

"And equally, they've got to get to know me, understand my position and where I like to be, what type of goalkeeper I am, so it's a lot of working it out on the pitch.

"I sometimes grab a conversation over lunch or in between reps and we're bouncing ideas off each other all the time."

London City's first test will come on September 4 as they open the WSL season against Man Utd at Hayes Lane, live on Sky Sports.

Earps' former side have had a turbulent summer, losing key players as well as changing head coach. Former Hearts boss Eva Olid replaced Marc Skinner , who left by mutual consent after five years.

"I was at Man Utd for five years. I have incredible memories there and met some incredible people," Earps said. "I know the club has changed a lot. There's not so many of the faces there that I know, but equally, they still have incredible players.

"It will be a really tough game, but I'm looking forward to it and I love a challenge. The support of Man Utd is always fantastic, home and away, so I know they'll come to Bromley and try and make it a difficult atmosphere for us.

"I don't know the ins and outs of everything, but I won an FA Cup with Marc and I will always really cherish that memory. It gives me goosebumps just thinking about it, to be honest.

"He also helped the club get to three other finals, so I think that speaks for itself and I wish him all the best in his next chapter."

Now though, Earps focus is on her own new chapter and another landmark chapter for London City. It remains to be seen how this headline-grabbing summer will translate onto the pitch - but it's one neither fans, nor the players, will forget in a hurry.

articles.title: El fichaje es Rashford: "Es uno de los nuestros y está viviendo su sueño"
articles.standfirst: Carrick le colocó de titular en la 'manita' ante el Ipswich y el ex del Barcelona volvió a brillar
articles.summary: Carrick le colocó de titular en la 'manita' ante el Ipswich y el ex del Barcelona volvió a brillar
articles.body: La decisión del Barcelona de no ejecutar la opción de compra de 30 millones de euros que tenía sobre Marcus Rashford (Mánchester, 1997) obligó al internacional inglés a regresar al Manchester United. Su elevado salario -cobra 17 millones de euros por temporada- complicó su salida de Old Trafford. Sin embargo, Michael Carrick, con el que compartió vestuario, parece dispuesto a darle una nueva oportunidad en el Manchester United. De hecho, Rashford fue una de las cuatro novedades que el técnico de los 'diablos rojos' introdujo en el once en la victoria sobre el Ipswich Town (5-2), después de caer contra el Hull City (2-0) en el estreno. Era su primera titularidad en Old Trafford en casi dos años, ¡¡¡desde diciembre de 2024!!! Disputó 80 minutos haciendo las veces de extremo izquierdo, con el '9' a la espalda, y, aunque no marcó ni asistió, dejó buenas sensaciones. Fue el segundo jugador del Man. United que más tiros a puerta realizó (2/4), que más regates completó (2/4), que más ocasiones generó (3) y el cuarto que más centros registró (3). También se aplicó en defensa. Fue el jugador de los 'diablos rojos' que más 'tackles' (entradas) completó con éxito (2/4). Recistró, además, tres recuperaciones y fue el segundo jugador que más duelos ganó (7/10). Una actuación que le valió para ganarse los elogios de Michael Carrick: "Estoy muy contento con Marcus. Creo que manejó todo el partido con normalidad. Estoy seguro de que fue agradable para él estar de vuelta, ser titular y disfrutar de formar parte de un buen equipo". "Creo que lo hizo particularmente bien en circunstancias difíciles. Ha aportado mucho al grupo, aunque resulte bastante obvio. Lo conozco desde hace tiempo. No estaba aquí cuando volví, pero ahora sí. Creo que está aprovechando al máximo esta oportunidad para nosotros y para él", insistió el entrenador de los 'diablos rojos'. No parece, salvo cambio drástico, que vaya a abandonar Old Trafford de aquí al final del mercado: “Es uno de los nuestros, está viviendo su sueño jugando aquí y tratando de tener éxito y ganar. Creo que hay jugadores que se han ido y han vuelto, y quizás jugadores que iban a irse pero no lo hicieron. Todo depende de lo que hagas después y de cuáles sean tus intenciones, y tengo que decir que ha estado fantástico desde que regresó". Omar Berrada, ex del City y ahora director general del United, también parece cerrarle la puerta de salida: "Esta tarde contaremos con nuestros nuevos fichajes Andrey (Santos), Youri (Tielemans), Karl (Darlow), Tynan (Thompson) y Carlos (Baleba). También nos complace dar la bienvenida de nuevo a Marcus al equipo". “Creemos que todos ellos contribuirán a mejorar la plantilla a medida que competimos en múltiples frentes. Nos espera una temporada apasionante y tenemos muchas ganas de volver a competir en la Liga de Campeones, donde hemos vivido tantas noches memorables en este magnífico estadio. Es donde siempre queremos estar”, remarcó Berrada.

articles.title: Daniel Munoz: Nottingham Forest complete £22m deal for right-back from Crystal Palace
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest complete the £22m signing of Daniel Munoz from Crystal Palace.
articles.body:
Nottingham Forest have completed the £22m signing of Daniel Munoz from Crystal Palace .

The Colombia right-back reunites with Oliver Glasner at the City Ground having won the FA Cup and Conference League together with the Eagles.

He has signed a three-year deal after spending the last two and a half years at Selhurst Park, scoring 11 goals in 109 appearances.

Munoz follows the £50m record arrival of Liam Delap and could make his debut against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League on Saturday.

He said: "I'm really excited because I can see so much talent, Forest is a team with great players, great qualities and great skills on the pitch, I can't wait to get out there so I can help my new team-mates and I think that we're going to do great things.

"It is a club that's fought hard in recent years, it has competed hard, it got to the semi-finals of the Europa League and I think it has even greater objectives for the future, and really this is what I like about Forest, and that's why I decided to come here."

Munoz, who has 51 caps, also helped Palace win the Community Shield in 2025.

Forest's chief football officer George Syrianos added: "Daniel has performed strongly in the Premier League and in European competition, and we believe he has the mentality and ambition to make a significant contribution to the club."

Forest drew 2-2 at Liverpool on Saturday, having lost their opening two games in the Premier League and Carabao Cup to Leeds United .

articles.title: Allan Elías, otro diamante brasileño para el City
articles.standfirst: El extremo de 22 años llega desde Palmeiras por unos 40 millones y firma hasta 2031 con el objetivo de seguir los pasos de Gabriel Jesus y triunfar en el Etihad
articles.summary: El extremo de 22 años llega desde Palmeiras por unos 40 millones y firma hasta 2031 con el objetivo de seguir los pasos de Gabriel Jesus y triunfar en el Etihad
articles.body: El Manchester City ha reforzado su plantilla con la incorporación del brasileño Allan Elías, una operación que queda pendiente de la autorización internacional. El futbolista, de 22 años, llega procedente del Palmeiras por unos 40 millones (38+2) y ha firmado un contrato por cinco temporadas, que le vinculará con la entidad inglesa hasta junio de 2031. Con este movimiento, el conjunto dirigido por Enzo Maresca suma una nueva pieza de futuro a un proyecto que continúa apostando por jóvenes talentos con gran proyección. Formado en una de las canteras más prestigiosas de Sudamérica, Allan ha destacado en el Palmeiras por su capacidad para desequilibrar en ataque, su velocidad y su calidad técnica. Aunque su posición habitual es la de extremo derecho, también puede desenvolverse en otras demarcaciones ofensivas e incluso retrasar su posición cuando las necesidades del equipo lo requieren, una versatilidad muy valorada en el fútbol moderno. El brasileño sigue así el camino de otros futbolistas del Palmeiras que dieron el salto a Europa y al propio Manchester City, como Gabriel Jesus en 2017 o el defensa Vitor Reis, incorporado por el club inglés en enero de 2025. Su llegada confirma la atención permanente de la entidad inglesa sobre el mercado sudamericano, donde continúa detectando algunos de los talentos más prometedores del panorama internacional. En sus primeras declaraciones como jugador citizen, Allan mostró su entusiasmo por afrontar este nuevo desafío. El futbolista calificó su fichaje como el momento más importante de su carrera y aseguró que las conversaciones mantenidas con los responsables del club le convencieron de que el Manchester City era el lugar idóneo para seguir creciendo. Además, prometió a la afición que dará el máximo esfuerzo para ganarse un puesto y ayudar al equipo a conquistar nuevos títulos. Por su parte, el director deportivo Hugo Viana elogió las cualidades del nuevo refuerzo y destacó tanto su talento como su capacidad de trabajo. El dirigente explicó que el City ha seguido de cerca su progresión en Brasil y considera que cuenta con el carácter necesario para triunfar en la Premier League. “Observamos su progresión en Brasil y vimos a un jugador que brilla en los momentos importantes y trabaja duro para el equipo con una actitud excelente", ha destacado el portugués. Con la llegada de Allan Elías, el campeón inglés incorpora a una de las jóvenes promesas del fútbol brasileño y añade más talento a una plantilla diseñada para competir al máximo nivel en todas las competiciones.

articles.title: Los dieciseisavos de la Copa Federación ya tienen emparejamientos
articles.standfirst: Los duelos, determinados por sorteo bajo criterios de proximidad geográfica, se disputarán entre el 8 y el 10 de septiembre
articles.summary: Los duelos, determinados por sorteo bajo criterios de proximidad geográfica, se disputarán entre el 8 y el 10 de septiembre
articles.body: La Copa Federación ya conoce el camino que deberán recorrer los 32 equipos que tratarán de proclamarse campeones, recogiendo el testigo del Ourense CF, vencedor de la pasada edición el pasado mes de noviembre. La Copa Federación se presenta, además, como un torneo que ofrece el acceso a la Copa de S. M. el Rey. El Salón Luis Aragonés de la Ciudad del Fútbol ha acogido este lunes el sorteo de los dieciseisavos de final, primera ronda de la fase nacional. Los 32 clubes clasificados, procedentes de las diferentes fases autonómicas, han quedado distribuidos en cuatro cuadros de ocho equipos cada uno. Los enfrentamientos se han configurado atendiendo a criterios de proximidad geográfica y los encuentros de dieciseisavos de final se disputarán entre el 8 y el 10 de septiembre Así, queda establecido el primer paso de un recorrido que continuará con los octavos y los cuartos de final dentro de cada uno de los cuatro cuadros. El ganador del cuadro A se enfrentará al vencedor del B en semifinales, mientras que el campeón del cuadro C hará lo propio con el del D. Cabe destacar que los cuatro semifinalistas tendrán un premio añadido: una plaza en la presente edición de la Copa de S. M. el Rey. Un camino que vuelve a presentarse como una oportunidad para que los clubes participantes puedan alcanzar uno de los grandes escenarios del fútbol nacional. articles.title: Una derrota que refuerza la idea de Ibai Gómez: "Ojalá seamos capaces de jugar así toda la temporada"
articles.standfirst: Técnico y plantilla quedaron satisfechos con el juego pese a caer en Tarragona
articles.summary: Técnico y plantilla quedaron satisfechos con el juego pese a caer en Tarragona
articles.body: Para volver a Segunda solo importan las victorias sin tener en cuenta el cómo. Sin embargo, para Ibai Gómez y su plantilla el estilo de juego va a dar más alegrías que tristezas. Y es que, tanto el técnico como sus jugadores quedaron dolidos con el resultado pero satisfecho con la imagen, ya que por ocasiones y dominio merecieron ganar. Eso sí, lo cierto es que no dominaron ninguna área pero ellos creen que es el camino a seguir. "Si juegas 20 partidos como este, ganas 19. Hemos sido absolutamente superiores y ha sido el mejor partido desde que estamos aquí. Me revienta perder pero ojalá seamos capaces de jugar así toda la temporada, ya que estaremos más cerca de lograr el objetivo. No me preocupa nada hoy más que el resultado. Tenemos muchas cosas que mejorar, pero estoy satisfecho", indicó el míster. Misma línea siguió Ander Herrera en el que fue su redebut con el Real Zaragoza: “No sé si en los últimos años el Real Zaragoza había jugado un partido generando tanto, sometiendo tanto al rival. Vamos a intentar jugar así siempre aunque es difícil jugar tan bien como hoy. Es complicado encontrar una explicación a lo que ha pasado hoy", señaló. El sábado reciben al Antequera en su primer partido en casa pero antes, mañana mismo, se cierra el mercado de fichajes y está por cerrar la contratación de un lateral derecho. Marco Sangalli, libre tras acabar su contrato con el Racing, es la opción preferida y las negociaciones han avanzado en las últimas horas. Además, Saidu finalmente se quedará en el club que ha rechazado las últimas ofertas.

articles.title: Daniel Munoz: Nottingham Forest sign defender from Crystal Palace in transfer deal worth up to £22m
articles.summary: Daniel Munoz has joined Nottingham Forest on a three-year deal with the option for a fourth; Palace opened the door for the 30-year-old's exit by signing Anan Khalaili from Union Saint-Gilloise; Palace have no plans to let Forest sign Dean Henderson as well
articles.body:
The deal for the right wing-back is understood to be worth up to £22m.

Munoz, who is reunited with former Palace boss Oliver Glasner at the City Ground, has joined on a three-year deal with the option for a fourth.

Palace opened the door for the 30-year-old's exit by signing Anan Khalaili from Union Saint-Gilloise. They secure a profit on a player they signed from Genk for £8.5m in January 2024.

Colombia international Munoz was a crucial player in Palace's Conference League and FA Cup triumphs.

Munoz told Forest's official website: "I'm really thankful. First of all, to God, for life, for another great opportunity, and to this management which has faith in my skill and my talent.

"I'm really excited and I can't wait to get out on the pitch so I can help my new teammates achieve all the objectives for this season.

"This is a winning club. I think that when this is the expectation, the mentality, both for the management and the technical team, and for the players, this makes it special.

"I think that Oliver Glasner is special, I have a very good relationship with him and we did big things together, it was an incredibly special period. What he did with our previous club, I have a lot of respect and a lot of admiration for him."

Could Henderson join Munoz at Nottingham Forest?

Crystal Palace have no plans to sell any more of their players to Nottingham Forest in the final days of the transfer window.

Last week, a report has emerged of a bid from Forest to sign Palace's goalkeeper and captain Dean Henderson.

But Sky Sports News has been told categorically that Henderson will not be allowed to depart before the deadline.

Palace plan to support new head coach Pierre Sage in the final days of the transfer window.

Are Forest planning anything else before the transfer deadline?

Nottingham Forest could make a late move for Newcastle forward Jacob Murphy .

Forest are keen on Murphy and are in the market for forwards amid the departure of Omari Hutchinson to AC Milan.

Newcastle have not formally been made aware yet but there is believed to have been interest from Forest earlier in the window, as well as Everton.

Newcastle are looking to add new forward options themselves with interest in Lille 's Matias Fernandes Pardo and Stuttgart's Bilal El Khannouss.

Meanwhile, Eintracht Frankfurt are in talks with Forest to re-sign Arnaud Kalimuendo on loan.

The striker was on loan at the German club for the second half of last season and they now want to do another loan potentially with an option to buy Kalimuendo permanently. He was left out of the matchday 18 on Saturday as Forest drew 2-2 at Liverpool.

Sky Sports News has already reported that Forest's proposed move for Harrison Armstrong from Everton has broken down.

After receiving an approach from Forest, Sky Sports News understands the board is unanimous in its decision to not sell the player.

What else are Palace working on before Deadline Day?

Crystal Palace are now close to an agreement with Atalanta to sign Honest Ahanor on loan.

Sky Sports News understands that the proposal is for Ahanor to join the Eagles on a season-long loan from Atalanta and then join Chelsea permanently next summer.

Chelsea have been in talks to sign him permanently from Atalanta for around £40m. He cannot be loaned from Chelsea to Palace because Axel Disasi is already on loan at Selhurst Park.

In terms of outgoings, Ismaila Sarr wants to leave Palace before the deadline. However, Palace insist the player is still not for sale and he still has a contract until 2029.

Liverpool made an approach for the Senegal international in the past week. He is one of a number of options under consideration at Liverpool, including Yankuba Minteh at Brighton.

Sarr has missed Palace's first two games of the season through injury. The window closes on Tuesday at 11pm.

articles.title: Glasner se lleva a Daniel Muñoz al Nottingham Forest
articles.standfirst: El ya exlateral derecho del Crystal Palace se marcha traspasado por 25,7 millones de euros
articles.summary: El ya exlateral derecho del Crystal Palace se marcha traspasado por 25,7 millones de euros
articles.body: Oliver Glasner no estará solo en el Nottingham Forest. El exentrenador del Crystal Palace se ha llevado con él a uno de los mejores laterales derechos de la Premier League: Daniel Muñoz (Amalfi, 1996). Sorprende, sobremanera, el precio del traspaso. El internacional colombiano, de 30 años, aterriza en el City Ground a cambio de 25,7 millones de euros, una cifra relativamente baja tratándose de la Liga inglesa. Muñoz, que recaló en el Crystal Palace en 2024 procedente del Genk previo pago de 8 millones de euros, se compromete por tres temporadas, hasta 2029, con el Forest. Atrás quedan los 11 goles y 16 asistencias que registró en 109 partidos con el Palace, con el que ganó tres títulos: la FA Cup (2024-25), la Community Shield (2025) y la Conference League (2025-26). "Estoy muy emocionado porque veo mucho talento. El Forest es un equipo con grandes jugadores, grandes cualidades y grandes habilidades en el campo. Tengo muchas ganas de salir a la cancha para poder ayudar a mis nuevos compañeros y creo que vamos a lograr grandes cosas", ha asegurado el ex de Águilas Doradas y Atlético Nacional. "Es un club que ha luchado mucho en los últimos años, ha competido con ahínco, llegó a las semifinales de la Europa League y creo que tiene objetivos aún mayores para el futuro, y eso es precisamente lo que me gusta del Forest, y por eso decidí venir aquí", ha reiterado Daniel Muñoz. "Daniel ha tenido un gran rendimiento en la Premier League y en competiciones europeas, y creemos que tiene la mentalidad y la ambición necesarias para hacer una contribución significativa al club", ha apuntado, por su parte, George Syrianos, director deportivo del Nottingham Forest.

articles.title: El Liverpool cumple el deseo de Iraola y convierte a Barcola en el reemplazo de Salah
articles.standfirst: El conjunto ‘red’ acuerda un traspaso de 145 millones de euros entre fijos y variables con el PSG · Supera a Neymar como la venta más cara del equipo dirigido por Luis Enrique
articles.summary: El conjunto ‘red’ acuerda un traspaso de 140 millones de euros con el PSG por el extremo francés
articles.body: La marcha de Mohamed Salah, a pesar de un último año que no hizo justicia a su leyenda, dejó un agujero de enormes dimensiones en la banda derecha de Anfield. Iraola llevaba todo el verano insistiendo en la obligación de cubrir esta necesidad y el Liverpool ha cumplido sus deseos: Bradley Barcola es nuevo jugador ‘red’ tras acordar un traspaso con el PSG que asciende hasta los 145 millones de euros... con variables incluidas. Fichado por 45 millones en el verano de 2023 procedente del Olympique de Lyon tras ‘romperla’ en el segundo tramo de temporada (siete goles y nueve asistencias) y brillar en el Europeo Sub21 con Francia (dos goles y dos asistencias), Barcola fue un jugador muy importante en el primer curso de Luis Enrique en el banquillo del Parque de los Príncipes. Integrado en el tridente junto a Mbappé y Dembélé, fue titular en 26 de los 39 partidos que disputó. Ya sin Kylian, se le exigía un paso al frente de cara a la siguiente temporada… y explotó firmando las mejores cifras (21 goles y 20 asistencias) de su carrera. Sin embargo, el ascenso de Doué y el fichaje de Kvaratskhelia en enero de 2025 le fueron restando cuota de protagonismo hasta arrancar como suplente en la final de la Champions contra el Bayern. Un panorama que no cambió de cara al curso pasado, donde a pesar de ser titular en 35 de 49 encuentros, siempre arrancó desde el banco en las noches importantes. Consciente de su situación, Barcola —ausente en la Supercopa de Europa, de Francia y en la primera jornada de la Ligue 1— solicitó un cambio de aires de cara a este verano. Ahora bien, el PSG no tenía necesidad alguna de transferir a su mejor revulsivo. Por ello, primero se cubrieron las espaldas con el fichaje de Mika Godts desde el Ajax y, posteriormente, han acordado un traspaso con el Liverpool para convertir al extremo francés en la mayor venta toda su historia. Supera, de este modo, los 90 millones que pagó Al Hilal por Neymar en 2023. Aunque sus mejores actuaciones han llegado desde la banda izquierda, es probable que Iraola quiera recuperar la versión de Barcola en derecha. Es decir, donde comenzó a destaparse con el Olympique de Lyon y la Sub21 de Francia. Esto permitiría que Víctor Muñoz, o en su defecto el joven Ngumoha, arrancasen desde su perfil predilecto. Todo, a la espera de saber qué ocurre con Gakpo y si habrá ofensiva por Minteh. Sea como fuere, el Liverpool ha cumplido los deseos del técnico de Usurbil con el fichaje de un extremo de primer nivel que, por cualidades, puede ser demoledor en la Premier.

articles.title: Marco Garcés: “El mercado está abierto y nosotros estamos moviéndonos”
articles.standfirst: El director de fútbol céltico no da por cerrada la plantilla a la que puede llegar Sebastián Cáceres
articles.summary: El director de fútbol céltico no da por cerrada la plantilla a la que puede llegar Sebastián Cáceres
articles.body: Marco Garcés, director de fútbol del Celta, trabaja intensamente para completar la plantilla antes de la medianoche de este martes: “El mercado está abierto. Nosotros estamos moviéndonos, estamos trabajando intensamente. No estamos planeando ninguna salida. Obviamente no sabes lo que puede llegar a suceder pero no estamos con ninguna salida planificada o ninguna salida en puerta y estamos intentando movernos para traer algún refuerzo". El que podría salir es Carles Pérez, futbolista transferible para club y cuerpo técnico, dijo: “Es una salida posible". No negó la llegada del central uruguayo de 27 años, procedente del América, Sebastián Cáceres: “Es una de las opciones que barajamos". Marco Garcés también se refirió al mal inicio de temporada: “Ha sido difícil. No iniciamos como hubiéramos querido pero estamos a un punto del inicio de la temporada pasada. Si logramos ganarle a la Real Sociedad estaríamos mejor que el año pasado. Creo que no es un motivo para levantar las alarmas porque estamos trabajando, tenemos mucha confianza en la plantilla tal cual está y buscaremos por ahí hacer algún retoque pero lo veo con un gran optimismo, con un gran entusiasmo. No fue el inicio que buscábamos pero no creo que sea un motivo de alarma”.

articles.title: With loaded field of potential Heisman Trophy-winning QBs, who will take it home?
articles.summary: The Heisman will almost assuredly be won by a quarterback this year. Is that because it's now a QB award, or is this crop of QBs just that good?
articles.body:
A quarterback is going to win the Heisman Trophy in December.

It's a preseason statement that's become prescient far more often than not in recent years. Over the past 16 years, Derrick Henry (2015), DeVonta Smith (2020) and Travis Hunter (2024) are the only three non-quarterbacks to win the award. Overall, only five non-quarterbacks have won the award since the turn of the century.

And the chances of a sixth non-quarterback winning in 2026 are incredibly slim.

Of the 27 players with 80-to-1 odds or better to win the Heisman at BetMGM, only two don't play quarterback. And those two players are teammates with a quarterback who has better odds to lift the trophy.

This upcoming college football season is positioned to be the year of the quarterback. Here's a look at how an incredibly deep group of quarterbacks stacks up ahead of the third season of the 12-team College Football Playoff .

Notre Dame QB CJ Carr (+750): The second-year starter is the favorite to win the award as Notre Dame looks certain to avoid an 0-2 start in 2026. Carr completed nearly 67% of his passes in 2025 and threw 24 TDs with just six interceptions. The Irish have the best odds of any team to go undefeated during the regular season and the offense should revolve around Carr even more in 2026 with the departures of running backs Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price to the NFL and a deep group of receivers on the roster.

Texas QB Arch Manning (+800): Manning opened the 2025 season as the Heisman favorite despite his relative lack of experience. He played in 10 games in 2024 and threw just 90 passes. Even he seemed perplexed at his status.

It was clear from Week 1 and a 14-7 loss to Ohio State that Manning had room to grow as a starter, and there were certainly some other rough moments — like a road loss to Florida. But Manning grew as the season went on, and closed 2025 with a flourish against Michigan, throwing for two scores and running for two others in a Citrus Bowl win. Given the way Texas has navigated the transfer portal, Manning shouldn't be counted on to run as much as he did in 2025, but improvements as a passer — and the addition of former Auburn WR Cam Coleman — should boost his passing numbers considerably.

Oregon QB Dante Moore (11-1): Moore was a surefire top-five pick in the 2026 NFL Draft but decided to play a third season at Oregon in 2026. That decision could make him the No. 1 draft pick in 2027. Moore will need to improve on the turnover issues that plagued him at times in 2026, but he still completed nearly 72% of his passes to a receiver unit that dealt with a lot of injuries throughout the season. The availability of players like Evan Stewart and Dakorien Moore could be massive for Moore's Heisman chances. The Ducks are our pick for the national title and a leap from Moore is a big reason why.

Ohio State QB Julian Sayin (12-1): Sayin briefly challenged former Oregon QB Bo Nix's record for completion percentage in 2025 before finishing the season at exactly 77%. Sayin had 301 completions on 391 throws for over 3,600 yards and 32 TDs. He doesn't offer much as a runner, but his efficiency as a passer was why he finished fourth in the Heisman voting.

He might have finished in the top three if he hadn't thrown for an interception in each of Ohio State's final two games and the Buckeyes' offense had scored more than 10 points in the Big Ten title game. Sayin then threw two more picks in the Buckeyes' playoff loss, so four of his eight interceptions across the entire season came in Ohio State's final three games.

Sayin's overall interception rate was still just 2%. And if he again has five games where he completes over 80% of his passes like he did last season, he's going to be in the mix again.

Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss (14-1): Chambliss finished eighth in the Heisman voting in 2025 after beginning the season as the Rebels' backup. He then won a court injunction to return for another season after the NCAA had counted a season he missed for healthy reasons at Division II Ferris State against his eligibility clock.

Chambliss threw for nearly 4,000 yards across 15 games in 2025 and had 30 total touchdowns. A repeat of those numbers will keep him as part of the Heisman discussion in 2026, and don't be surprised if Chambliss takes over as a September favorite with a big game against LSU and former head coach Lane Kiffin in Week 3.

Miami QB Darian Mensah (11-1): The former Duke quarterback pledged to return to the ACC champions in 2026 before a big offer from the Hurricanes wooed him away and led to a settlement so Mensah could head south and play for the team that made it to the national title game despite missing out on the ACC championship.

Miami has done pretty well with transfer quarterbacks lately, too. Cam Ward parlayed his only season with the Hurricanes into a fourth-place finish in the Heisman voting in 2024 and the No. 1 pick in the 2025 NFL Draft while Carson Beck threw for over 3,800 yards and played his best football over the second half of last season as the Hurricanes made their playoff push. If Miami is a national title contender again, it's because its offense will be even better and more like the one that Ward led in 2024.

Indiana QB Josh Hoover (15-1): Fernando Mendoza led Indiana to an undefeated national championship season and the Heisman Trophy in his only season at Indiana in 2025. That's a pretty high standard for Hoover.

After Kurtis Rourke led Indiana to the College Football Playoff in 2024, the Hoosiers look set to make it a third time with a third different transfer quarterback. The three-year starter at TCU has thrown for nearly 10,000 career yards and 71 touchdowns while averaging over 8 yards an attempt. Like Mendoza, Indiana receivers Omar Cooper Jr. and Elijah Sarratt are also off to the NFL, but Charlie Becker is back after his breakout late in the season and Michigan State transfer Nick Marsh should get a high number of targets right away.

LSU QB Sam Leavitt (20-1): Leavitt is looking to bounce back from an injury-wrecked 2025 that was on track to be much worse than his breakout 2024 season. The Michigan State transfer led Arizona State to a Big 12 title and the College Football Playoff two seasons ago as he threw for over 2,800 yards and rushed for 443 more with 29 total touchdowns. Across seven games in 2025, Leavitt completed less than 61% of his passes and averaged just 6.8 yards an attempt.

If Leavitt is going to be a Heisman contender in 2026, it's because LSU is immediately a national title contender under Kiffin. And Leavitt is putting up numbers similar to Chambliss and Jaxson Dart.

Georgia QB Gunner Stockton (20-1): Stockton finished seventh in the voting a season ago as he completed nearly 70% of his passes and threw for 24 TDs while rushing for 10 more. Stockton had very good numbers — but it was also easy to see how he got a Heisman bump for being the starting quarterback of the SEC champions.

If Stockton is going to move in from the periphery of the Heisman discussion, he'll probably have to throw for more than 3,000 yards and have 40 total touchdowns while Georgia makes it to the SEC championship game yet again.

USC QB Jayden Maiava (20-1): If you think this is the year for USC to be a true contender in the Big Ten, Maiava is a great bet. After all, Lincoln Riley's teams lost just nine regular-season games from 2017 through 2022 as Baker Mayfield, Kyler Murray and Caleb Williams each won the Heisman and Jalen Hurts finished second. In his first season at USC in 2025, Maiava threw for over 3,700 yards and had 30 total touchdowns. He shined in the Trojans' Week Zero win with nearly 300 passing yards and three total touchdowns before being taken out for the final quarter in an easy win over San Jose State.

Oklahoma QB John Mateer (25-1): Mateer was the early-season favorite for the Heisman before a thumb injury derailed his season. It's perfectly reasonable to expect his numbers in 2026 to be much more like they were in September than they were after the injury. After all, Mateer threw for 29 TDs and rushed for 15 more in 2024 at Washington State. Wins at Michigan and Georgia in September could make Mateer the favorite when October rolls around once again.

Texas A&M QB Marcel Reed (30-1): Reed was never a Heisman favorite in 2025 but was certainly heading toward a top-10 finish before a rough end to the season. With former offensive coordinator Collin Klein now the head coach at Kansas State, Reed has the chance to really shine if the Aggies can avoid having their SEC title game hopes derailed in the final weeks of the regular season again.

Alabama QB Keelon Russell (25-1): Russell has appeared in just two college football games but is among the favorites after he was named Alabama's starting quarterback ahead of the Crimson Tide's opener against East Carolina. The former five-star recruit could put up stats similar to Jalen Milroe if Alabama is among the SEC's elite again.

Texas Tech QB Will Hammond (40-1): Hammond's odds are relatively low even though Texas Tech did its best to find an upgrade at quarterback in Brendan Sorsby while Hammond is also recovering from a torn ACL suffered during the 2025 season. That's because Texas Tech is the undisputed favorite for the Big 12 title and has what looks to be an incredibly easy schedule. The Red Raiders added former Florida State and Boston College quarterback Thomas Castellanos last week as insurance.

Michigan QB Bryce Underwood (40-1): Russell was the No. 2 recruit in the high school class of 2025. Underwood was No. 1. The Michigan native showed just how far he has to go as a passer in 2025, but he has the talent to get there. And he's also better positioned for success in 2026 under new head coach Kyle Whittingham and offensive coordinator Jason Beck. With that same coaching staff, Utah QBs Devon Dampier and Byrd Ficklin combined for 47 TDs in 2025.

Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith (14-1): It's entirely conceivable that Smith could end up ahead of Sayin in the Heisman odds, especially if he somehow becomes even more dominant in 2026. Despite missing a game against Rutgers and being limited late in the season with a strained quad, Smith still had 87 catches for 1,243 yards and 12 scores in 2025. One-hundred catches is definitely on the table in 2026.

Miami WR Malachi Toney (40-1): Toney opened his college career with six catches for 82 yards and a TD in Miami's Week 1 win over Notre Dame. That established him as the best freshman offensive player in college football as he led Miami with 109 catches for 1,211 yards and 10 TDs. With Cooper Barkate, Duke's leading receiver in 2025, playing alongside him, defenses can't exclusively focus on Toney in 2026.

articles.title: Why Atlético are acquiring Jonathan David to complete Simeone’s attack
articles.summary: Atlético de Madrid on Monday agreed with Juventus on a loan move for Canada striker Jonathan David, according to multiple outlets. First reported by Marca’s...
articles.body:
Atlético de Madrid on Monday agreed with Juventus on a loan move for Canada striker Jonathan David, according to multiple outlets.

First reported by Marca's Diego Pico and later corroborated by Relevo's Marcos Durán as well as the football influencer Fabrizio Romano , David will join Atlético — who held interest in him when he played for Lille — on an initial loan with a €25 million option to buy. It is not an obligatory buy clause based on appearances or other milestones, which means Atleti and Juve will avoid a standoff like the one that developed over Nico González late last season.

In addition, Juve are covering "a significant portion" of David's €11 million gross salary. That factor undoubtedly convinced Mateu Alemany to pursue this deal instead of one for Newcastle's Nick Woltemade, who appears to be on his way to Turin as David's replacement.

The 26-year-old David joined Juve just last summer following five superb seasons at Lille, where he helped Les Dogues to a Ligue 1 title in 2021 and scored 109 goals across 232 appearances in all competitions — including 77 in 135 games over his final three seasons. But David struggled mightily in Italy; he scored only eight goals in 46 appearances last season, and he was whistled off the pitch during the Old Lady's 2-0 home win over Parma at the weekend. At the FIFA World Cup over the summer, David scored a hat trick for Canada in a 6-0 win over Qatar during the group stage, but he did not score again as the co-hosts were eliminated in the round of 16.

David appeals to Atlético as a low-cost distressed asset seeking to turn his career around. The financial aspect is key given that the club still has to pay Josema Giménez and Thomas Lemar's salaries for 2026/27; according to Marca, neither player will leave Atlético this summer, meaning the club is on the hook for roughly €10 million in gross wages between them. Their refusal to leave — as is their contractual right — afforded Alemany less room to maneuver in the market.

Moreover, David's profile as a player makes it easy to see how Diego Simeone can "recover" him after a down year at Juventus. David is a fast, technical forward who combines well with others; he struggled at Juventus when he was forced into a role as a pure number nine and was asked to be a self-sufficient goal source. That's not really who David is; assuming Julián Alvarez stays, Simeone will continue to count on his compatriot to be that attacker who conjures goals out of nothing.

articles.title: Bradley Barcola to Liverpool: France forward who has moved from PSG is quick, strong, versatile, intelligent
articles.summary: Is Bradley Barcola a good signing for Liverpool? Having spoken to the former Paris Saint-Germain forward's old academy boss, Adam Bate examines the strengths and weaknesses of the France international to find out more…
articles.body:
The 23-year-old France international has won the Champions League with PSG back to back but had to be content with coming off the bench in both finals. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia's arrival from Napoli in January of 2025 established him as first choice on the left.

But just because Barcola was not a guaranteed starter in Paris does not mean he is not a guaranteed star. This is a player with pace, physicality and intelligence, someone whose skills have been honed under Luis Enrique. With Barcola, the potential is as vast as the fee.

For a player so highly rated, Barcola's rise has been serendipitous. At Lyon, he was on the fringes of the first team under France legend Laurent Blanc until a player exit changed everything. "That was a turning point," Jean-Francois Vulliez told Sky Sports .

"A club in Switzerland was interested because he was not playing for the first team. At that time, Blanc was the coach and we had Karl Toko Ekambi. But he decided he wanted to leave so the coach decided to stop the loan because we might need Bradley.

Vulliez explained: "It was a key moment because he realised that if Toko Ekambi left, Bradley could be a solution and there was an opportunity to use him. Toko Ekambi did leave. Bradley stayed. One match later, there was an injury and Laurent needed him."

Having worked with Barcola as a boy in Lyon's academy, Vulliez knows him well. In fact, he actually followed Barcola to PSG and now works as a development coach for the French and European champions. In his job, he has seen plenty of standout youngsters.

But Barcola was not necessarily one of them. He was a talent, for sure. But this level of success? That was not obvious. "He was a normal kid, he never played above his age category, never jumped a stage. His maturation was a normal process," he explained.

"It is an interesting pathway because every player is different. Sometimes, there are players like [Kylian] Mbappe who mature very early. Others need time. Bradley never played for France's age-group teams. He was a good player but not physically ready.

"We were very patient with him at Lyon because we knew he had the skills, we just had to wait for that maturation process, that psychological maturation, that physical maturation. When that transformation eventually happens, they will improve quickly."

Following Toko Ekambi's exit, Barcola scored five goals in nine games in early 2023 and after impressing for his country at that summer's European U21 Championship, there came a protracted move to PSG. "His body was in Lyon but his head was in Paris."

The three seasons that have followed have brought 13 trophies and 39 goals in over 150 appearances. Under Luis Enrique, he adapted his game, taking much better care of the ball than before. Barcola knows when to run at defences and when to keep it simple.

The player that Barcola is today is a product of that understated youth career. A late developer physically, dominating defenders was not an option as a teenager. That forced him into finding other ways. "He developed his intelligence," pointed out Vulliez.

"He was able to scan the pitch, take good information and use the space. Very early, he had this and he had speed. Then, he progressed with his muscles, became powerful. It is a combination of these tactical abilities, technical abilities and physical abilities."

Barcola was used primarily as a left-sided wide forward at PSG. But his instincts are closer to that of a striker than a winger. Indeed, he played up front at Lyon until the age of 17. From that flank, he can cut inside and shoot into the far corner with his stronger foot.

They are instincts that are hard to teach and top clubs cherish those in wide positions who possess them because it is not enough to look good - players need numbers. Barcola is balanced, in this sense, because he can score goals and create chances for others.

This graphic highlights his impressive shot volume for PSG, ranking among the top 10 players in Ligue 1 per 90 minutes last season. Playing wide does not stop him. "He is very clever with his runs inside." The timing of those movements is an important trait.

"Because he played as a striker, he retains that ability to know when he needs to come inside and when he needs to run beyond. With Bradley in your team, you need to use this capacity to come between the lines or run from deep, because it is his strength.

"We never had a problem with him at the academy because he is intelligent and listens so when you are the coach that makes it easier to manage him because he can adapt to whatever strategy the coach wants to use. He understands because he is clever.

"I do not think you can transform a player after the age of 17 because if the player does not have the intelligence at that age then they will never have it. That is why it is vital to develop this intelligence early. Bradley has it. You can adapt his position later."

More will be demanded as he progresses. His finishing can be a little lax. Enrique has pushed him to become more clinical. But there is time. "There are many very good players who improved their finishing when they became more mature," said Vulliez.

"As with every young player, sometimes they need that push but he has the mind to do it and that makes it easier. Maybe the left wing is the better position for him right now but I am curious to see how he develops because I believe he is able to become a No 9."

That flexibility makes him appealing. Barcola has operated on the right too and has the pace to get to the byline if that is what the coach wants from him. He ranked among the top 10 fastest players in the Champions League last season. He can play knock and run.

He is a better player than the one who arrived in Paris, better too than the prospect in Lyon's academy. "Nobody could have imagined this," Vulliez conceded. The question now being asked by clubs regarding Barcola is how much better he could still become.
